habitat: Singly or in pairs in various types of woodland and in suburbia, often in wattle trees. It creeps along branches, perches like a passerine, or hops on the ground with its tail raised.
summary: A common, localised resident. It is identified by a rust-brown patch on the throat and upper breast, and by brown-speckled upperparts with a blackish broken line from the crown to the mantle. The underparts below that patch are creamy-white. The call is a high-pitched kek-kek-kek-kek. Sexes were not separated. It uses a natural hole or an old barbet or woodpecker hole, and it lacks the stiff tail of a woodpecker. The Kemp paper name Redthroated Wryneck and the code RB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Cardinal Woodpecker has a straight pointed bill, a stiff tail and a streaked breast, and it braces on trunks. The wryneck has a rust-brown throat, speckled upperparts and perches more like a passerine.

head.pattern: Blackish broken line from the crown to the mantle. Newman says rust-brown on the throat and upper breast. The colour list has no rust, so those parts are stored as rufous.

underparts.pattern: Rust-brown throat and upper breast on creamy-white.

tail.shape: Raised when the bird hops on the ground. Newman says it lacks the strong supporting tail of a woodpecker.

research.note: Newman calls it a common, localised resident, and Avibase does not mark the Kruger occurrence rare or accidental, so status is resident and all twelve months are listed. Sexes were not separated, so one adult description is shared and the sex table follows that. The immature was not described. Bill colour, eye, legs and wings were not given. Newman says rust-brown. That colour is not in the vocabulary, so the throat and breast are stored as rufous. No Kruger photograph was found under an allowed licence. The side and front are from Addo, and the back is a CC0 frame from the Uitenhage district that also includes a second bird. No flight photograph was found. The grade A call is from Port Alfred. Population figures, the Kemp paper name Redthroated Wryneck and the code RB were left unchanged.
